target_customer: Talented graduates and early career people who want a high impact career; funded by philanthropic donors, not users
problem: Career advice rarely asks which paths do the most good. 80,000 Hours gives free research, a guide, a job board and one on one advice.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by philanthropic grants, mainly Open Philanthropy; all advice is free

founders.name: Benjamin Todd
education: Oxford (per 80,000 Hours about page, recent Oxford graduate)
founders.background_notes: The YC launch post says he was a student when he met his cofounder.

founders.name: William MacAskill
education: Oxford (per about page, recent Oxford graduate)
founders.background_notes: YC launch post of August 2015 describes him as an associate professor of philosophy at Oxford.

technical_complexity.rationale: A content website, podcast and advising service. The hard part is research quality, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Reputation, a large audience in effective altruism and a deep body of research are hard to copy quickly, but the content is free and replicable by other nonprofits.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it. It was a project of Effective Ventures and spun out as an independent organisation, completed in 2025.

market_need_then: The founders say an early 2011 lecture led audience members to change career plans and ask for an organisation; the organisation reports thousands of self reported career plan changes.

branding.name_origin: The name refers to the roughly 80,000 hours in a typical career (40 years x 50 weeks x 40 hours), the biggest decision for impact according to Ben Todd.
branding.brand_signature: The 80,000 hours framing of a career
branding.community_and_virality: Large effective altruism community following, a podcast and a career guide published as a book (a Penguin Random House edition is cited on its about page).

brand_strength.rationale: The name encodes the pitch and is widely recognized in effective altruism and among graduates; Todd concedes it is slightly misleading since careers are a series of steps.

pivots.to: Helping people navigate the transition to a world with powerful AI
pivots.why: Strategy shift stated on the about page in early 2025

outcome_analysis: 80,000 Hours began in 2011, joined YC as a nonprofit in summer 2015 and has grown to a team of more than 50 funded mostly by Open Philanthropy. It succeeded as a mission driven brand with steady grants, spun out of Effective Ventures in 2025 and refocused on AI. There is no equity outcome, so the story is durable donor funded growth built on a memorable name and a clear audience.
notes: Grant amounts come from Open Philanthropy and Good Ventures grant pages as shown in search results (pages not opened individually). Other Open Philanthropy grants exist (2017 $1.125M, 2022 $3M marketing, 2023 about $5.58M, 2025 $2.7M marketing) but are not itemized here. Total funding is not stated by the company. YC launch post names no competitors and no dated competitor sources were found. Spin-out completion is dated April 1, 2025 by the about page and May 2025 by the post. Added Open Philanthropy grants from the Longterm Wiki grant tracker, which reproduces the Open Philanthropy (now Coefficient Giving) grant database; the original Open Philanthropy pages now redirect, so each added round rests on this single third-party tracker: 510K Feb 2018 general support, 3,457,284 Feb 2020 general support, 1.25M May 2022 general support, 3M Jun 2022 marketing, 2,492,000 Apr 2023 marketing (the audit said about 2.49M), 2.4M Oct 2023 marketing and 2.7M Feb 2025 marketing. Not itemized: the 2017 1.125M, Jan 2023 1.2M and May 2023 5,575,238 general support grants. The 2022 to 2025 marketing grants are earmarked for advertising spend.
